learningObjectives.title: Waves in air, fluids and solids

questions.q: In a transverse wave, the oscillations are:
options: Parallel to the direction of energy transfer
Perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer
In the same plane as compressions and rarefactions
Always in the direction of wave travel
questions.explain: In a transverse wave the oscillations are perpendicular (at right angles) to the direction of energy transfer.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a longitudinal wave?
options: Ripple on the surface of water
questions.explain: Sound waves are longitudinal, consisting of compressions and rarefactions along the direction of travel.

questions.q: The amplitude of a wave is:
options: The maximum displacement of a point from its rest position
The distance between two adjacent peaks
The number of waves passing a point each second
The time taken for one complete oscillation
questions.explain: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of a point on the wave from its undisturbed (rest) position.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the wavelength of a wave?
options: The distance from one point on a wave to the equivalent point on the next wave
The height of a wave crest above the rest position
The number of complete waves produced each second
The speed at which the wave travels through a medium
questions.explain: Wavelength is the distance from a point on one wave to the equivalent point on the adjacent wave, e.g. crest to crest.

questions.q: Which equation correctly links wave speed, frequency and wavelength?
questions.explain: The wave equation is v = f λ, so wave speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength.

questions.q: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 2 m. What is its speed?
questions.explain: Using v = f λ = 50 x 2 = 100 m/s.

questions.q: A sound wave travels at 340 m/s with a frequency of 170 Hz. What is its wavelength?
questions.explain: Rearranging v = f λ gives λ = v / f = 340 / 170 = 2 m.

questions.q: A wave has a frequency of 25 Hz. What is its period?
A wave has a period of 0.02 s. What is its frequency?
questions.explain: Frequency f = 1 / T = 1 / 0.02 = 50 Hz.

questions.q: Electromagnetic waves are:
options: A mixture of transverse and longitudinal waves
Waves that require a medium to travel
questions.explain: All electromagnetic waves are transverse and can travel through a vacuum.

questions.q: Which type of electromagnetic wave has the lowest frequency?
questions.explain: Radio waves have the lowest frequency (and longest wavelength) of the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.q: Which type of electromagnetic wave has the highest frequency and shortest wavelength?
questions.explain: Gamma rays have the highest frequency and shortest wavelength in the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.q: How do the speeds of radio waves and X-rays compare in a vacuum?
options: They travel at the same speed of about 3 x 10^8 m/s
Radio waves travel faster because they have a longer wavelength
X-rays travel faster because they have a higher frequency
Their speeds cannot be compared without knowing the source
questions.explain: All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed of about 3 x 10^8 m/s through a vacuum.

questions.q: When a wave passes from one medium into another and changes direction, this is called refraction. It happens because:
options: The wave changes speed at the boundary
The wave loses all of its energy
The frequency of the wave increases
questions.explain: Refraction occurs because the wave changes speed as it crosses the boundary between two media, changing its direction (unless it hits along the normal).

questions.q: Radio waves can be produced by:
options: Changes within the nucleus of an atom
Electrons falling between energy levels only
questions.explain: Radio waves are produced by oscillations (alternating currents) in electrical circuits.

questions.q: Which is a common use of microwaves?
options: Producing images of the inside of the body using ionising radiation
questions.explain: Microwaves are used for satellite communications (and for heating food in microwave ovens).

questions.q: Why can sound waves not travel through a vacuum?
options: There are no particles to vibrate and pass on the wave
They travel too quickly to be detected
A vacuum absorbs all sound energy
Sound waves are transverse and need a solid surface
questions.explain: Sound is a longitudinal wave that needs particles of a medium to vibrate, so it cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.q: Which electromagnetic wave from the Sun is mainly responsible for causing sunburn and increasing the risk of skin cancer?
questions.explain: Ultraviolet radiation is ionising and can damage skin cells, causing sunburn and increasing skin cancer risk.

questions.q: A perfect black body is an object that:
options: Absorbs all of the radiation incident on it
Reflects all of the radiation incident on it
Emits no radiation at any temperature
questions.explain: A perfect black body absorbs all radiation incident on it and is also the best possible emitter of radiation.

questions.q: As the temperature of a body increases, how does the radiation it emits change?
options: It emits more radiation and the peak shifts to shorter wavelengths
It emits less radiation and the peak shifts to longer wavelengths
The amount and wavelength of radiation stay the same
questions.explain: As temperature rises a body emits radiation across more wavelengths at greater intensity, and the peak intensity moves to shorter wavelengths.
